Here’s a truly advanced Keras project—this time implementing self-supervised contrastive learning (SimCLR) on the CIFAR-10 dataset. It’s a big leap from typical CNN-based classification. The full code dominates the answer, with brief framing and notes following.

🧠 Project Title

ai-ml-ds-SrmZNuoOhMk – Self-Supervised Visual Representation Learning with SimCLR
Filename: simclr_self_supervised_cifar10.py

# simclr_self_supervised_cifar10.py

import tensorflow as tf
from tensorflow import keras
from tensorflow.keras import layers
import numpy as np
import datetime
import os

# 1. Hyperparams and config
batch_size: int = 256
img_size: int = 32
projection_dim: int = 128
temperature: float = 0.5
epochs: int = 50
seed: int = 42
num_examples: int = 50000

# 2. Data loading & augmentation
(cifar_images_raw, _), _ = keras.datasets.cifar10.load_data()
cifar_images: np.ndarray = cifar_images_raw.astype("float32") / 255.0

def get_augmenter():
    return keras.Sequential([
        layers.RandomFlip("horizontal"),
        layers.RandomRotation(0.2),
        layers.RandomZoom(0.2, 0.2),
    ], name="data_augmenter")

augmenter = get_augmenter()

def simclr_augment(x: tf.Tensor) -> tf.Tensor:
    view1 = augmenter(x, training=True)
    view2 = augmenter(x, training=True)
    return view1, view2

dataset = tf.data.Dataset.from_tensor_slices(cifar_images)
dataset = dataset.shuffle(num_examples, seed=seed)
dataset = dataset.map(simclr_augment, num_parallel_calls=tf.data.AUTOTUNE)
dataset = dataset.batch(batch_size).prefetch(tf.data.AUTOTUNE)

# 3. Build encoder + projection head
base_model = keras.applications.ResNet50(
    include_top=False, input_shape=(img_size, img_size, 3), pooling="avg"
)
base_model.trainable = True

encoder_input = layers.Input((img_size, img_size, 3))
representation: tf.Tensor = base_model(encoder_input, training=True)
projection: tf.Tensor = layers.Dense(256, activation="relu")(representation)
projection: tf.Tensor = layers.Dense(projection_dim)(projection)
encoder = keras.Model(encoder_input, projection, name="encoder")

# 4. Contrastive loss
def nt_xent_loss(zi, zj, temperature):
    zi = tf.math.l2_normalize(zi, axis=1)
    zj = tf.math.l2_normalize(zj, axis=1)
    representations = tf.concat([zi, zj], axis=0)
    similarity_matrix = tf.matmul(representations, representations, transpose_b=True)
    mask = tf.eye(2 * batch_size)
    logits = similarity_matrix / temperature
    logits_mask = tf.cast(1 - mask, dtype=tf.bool)
    logits = tf.boolean_mask(logits, logits_mask)
    logits = tf.reshape(logits, (2 * batch_size, -1))
    positive_samples = tf.concat(
        [tf.linalg.diag_part(similarity_matrix, k=batch_size),
         tf.linalg.diag_part(similarity_matrix, k=-batch_size)], axis=0
    )[:, None] / temperature
    loss = tf.nn.softmax_cross_entropy_with_logits(
        labels=tf.one_hot(tf.zeros(2 * batch_size, dtype=tf.int32), logits.shape[1]),
        logits=tf.concat([positive_samples, logits], axis=1)
    )
    return tf.reduce_mean(loss)

# 5. Training loop
optimizer = keras.optimizers.Adam()

@tf.function
def train_step(view1, view2):
    with tf.GradientTape() as tape:
        zi = encoder(view1, training=True)
        zj = encoder(view2, training=True)
        loss = nt_xent_loss(zi, zj, temperature)
    grads = tape.gradient(loss, encoder.trainable_variables)
    optimizer.apply_gradients(zip(grads, encoder.trainable_variables))
    return loss

for epoch in range(1, epochs + 1):
    total_loss: float = 0.0
    num_batches: int = 0
    for batch in dataset:
        v1, v2 = batch
        loss_value = train_step(v1, v2)
        total_loss += loss_value
        num_batches += 1
    print(f"[{datetime.datetime.now():%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S}] Epoch {epoch}/{epochs}, Loss: {total_loss/num_batches:.4f}")

# 6. Save encoder
encoder.save("simclr_encoder_cifar10.h5")
print("Encoder saved.")

✅ Example Use-Cases / Test Inputs

  • Load two augmented views: x = cifar_images[0:1] v1, v2 = simclr_augment(x)
  • Train for 1 epoch to check training loop; inspect loss.
  • Load saved encoder and fine‑tune classifier on small labeled subset.
